m1_content = '''"""Tests for milestone m1: add_completion_class return value fix."""

import pytest


def test_add_completion_class_returns_cls():
    """The decorator should return the class itself, not None."""
    import click.shell_completion as sc

    class MyBashClass(sc.ShellComplete):
        name = "mybash"
        source_template = ""

        def get_completion_args(self):
            raise NotImplementedError

        def format_completion(self, item):
            raise NotImplementedError

    result = sc.add_completion_class(MyBashClass)
    assert result is MyBashClass, f"Expected MyBashClass but got {result}"


def test_add_completion_class_as_decorator():
    """Using @add_completion_class should leave the class intact and callable."""
    import click.shell_completion as sc

    class MyZshClass(sc.ShellComplete):
        name = "myzsh"
        source_template = ""

        def get_completion_args(self):
            raise NotImplementedError

        def format_completion(self, item):
            raise NotImplementedError

    decorated = sc.add_completion_class(MyZshClass)
    # The returned object must be the same class
    assert decorated is MyZshClass
    # The class must still be callable (instantiable)
    instance = decorated(None, {}, "test", "_TEST")
    assert isinstance(instance, MyZshClass)


def test_add_completion_class_return_equals_retrieved():
    """The return value of add_completion_class must equal the class retrieved from registry."""
    import click.shell_completion as sc

    class MyFishClass(sc.ShellComplete):
        name = "myfish"
        source_template = ""

        def get_completion_args(self):
            raise NotImplementedError

        def format_completion(self, item):
            raise NotImplementedError

    result = sc.add_completion_class(MyFishClass)
    retrieved = sc.get_completion_class("myfish")
    # Both must be the class itself, not None
    assert result is MyFishClass, f"add_completion_class returned {result}, expected MyFishClass"
    assert retrieved is MyFishClass, f"get_completion_class returned {retrieved}, expected MyFishClass"
    assert result is retrieved, "Return value and registry lookup must both resolve to the class"


def test_add_completion_class_with_custom_name():
    """The decorator can register under a custom name string and return the class."""
    import click.shell_completion as sc

    class CustomShell(sc.ShellComplete):
        name = "defaults_to_this"
        source_template = ""

        def get_completion_args(self):
            raise NotImplementedError

        def format_completion(self, item):
            raise NotImplementedError

    result = sc.add_completion_class(CustomShell, name="custom_name")
    assert result is CustomShell, f"Expected CustomShell but got {result}"
    retrieved = sc.get_completion_class("custom_name")
    assert retrieved is CustomShell
'''

with open('crucible_hidden/test_m1.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(m1_content)

m2_content = '''"""Tests for milestone m2: dots replaced with underscores in completion variable name."""

import pytest


def test_prog_name_dots_replaced_in_env_var():
    """A prog_name with dots should produce an env var with underscores, not dots."""
    import click
    from click.testing import CliRunner
    from click.core import Group, Command

    cli = Group("my.app", commands=[Command("sub")])
    runner = CliRunner()
    result = runner.invoke(cli, env={"_MY_APP_COMPLETE": "bash_source"})
    # The generated script should reference _MY_APP_COMPLETE, not _MY.APP_COMPLETE
    assert "_MY_APP_COMPLETE" in result.output, (
        f"Expected _MY_APP_COMPLETE in output but got:\\n{result.output}"
    )
    assert "_MY.APP_COMPLETE" not in result.output, (
        f"Output should not contain dots in env var name:\\n{result.output}"
    )


def test_prog_name_multiple_dots_all_replaced():
    """Multiple dots in prog_name should all be replaced with underscores."""
    import click
    from click.testing import CliRunner
    from click.core import Group, Command

    cli = Group("my.app.name", commands=[Command("sub")])
    runner = CliRunner()
    result = runner.invoke(cli, env={"_MY_APP_NAME_COMPLETE": "bash_source"})
    # All dots should be replaced
    assert "_MY_APP_NAME_COMPLETE" in result.output, (
        f"Expected _MY_APP_NAME_COMPLETE in output but got:\\n{result.output}"
    )
    assert "." not in result.output.split("_COMPLETE")[0].split("=")[-1] if "_COMPLETE" in result.output else True, (
        f"No dots should remain in env var portion:\\n{result.output}"
    )


def test_prog_name_dashes_and_dots_combined():
    """Prog_name with both dashes and dots should have both converted to underscores."""
    import click
    from click.testing import CliRunner
    from click.core import Group, Command

    cli = Group("my-app.cli", commands=[Command("sub")])
    runner = CliRunner()
    result = runner.invoke(cli, env={"_MY_APP_CLI_COMPLETE": "bash_source"})
    # Both dashes and dots should be underscores
    assert "_MY_APP_CLI_COMPLETE" in result.output, (
        f"Expected _MY_APP_CLI_COMPLETE in output but got:\\n{result.output}"
    )
    # No dots or dashes should appear in the env var portion
    complete_section = result.output
    assert ".COMPLETE" not in complete_section, (
        f"Dots should not appear before COMPLETE:\\n{complete_section}"
    )


def test_completion_resolves_subcommands_with_dot_prog_name():
    """When the env var is set to complete mode, subcommands should resolve."""
    import os
    import click
    from click.testing import CliRunner
    from click.core import Group, Command

    cli = Group("my.app", commands=[Command("sub"), Command("other")])
    runner = CliRunner()

    env = {
        "_MY_APP_COMPLETE": "bash_complete",
        "COMP_WORDS": "",
        "COMP_CWORD": "0",
    }
    result = runner.invoke(cli, env=env)
    # Should return completions for subcommands
    assert "plain" in result.output.lower(), (
        f"Expected completion items in output but got:\\n{result.output}"
    )
    # Subcommand names should appear
    assert "sub" in result.output or "other" in result.output, (
        f"Expected subcommand names in output but got:\\n{result.output}"
    )
'''

    f.write(m2_content)

print("test_m2.py rewritten")
